header:
Date: 2027-03-05
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Enabled
Attendees: Marco Alvarez (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (CTO - Summit Labs), James Kim (Infra), Lara Chen (Data Sci), Tom Weaver (Procurement)
summary: Intro discovery for Summit Labs evaluating Redwood for a mixed-hosting strategy: start with Redwood hosted quickstart using free credits to validate model fit and latency, then pilot Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for PII workloads. Main concerns: latency to EU customers, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/compliance, and predictable unit costs. Agreed next steps: send credits redemption, share deployment checklist and pricing, collect traffic profile, and schedule pilot benchmark in three weeks.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment decision factors
Pilot scope and success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, availability)
Integration points (SDK, server-side calls, embedding/semantic search)
transcript:
00:00 Marco: hey everyone thanks for joining, we kept it to 45-ish minutes — thanks Priya for the intro. can you hear me ok?
00:04 Priya: yep hearing you, thanks Marco. we just wanted a quick walkthrough of what Redwood could look like for Summit, we have a few options on the table so trying to narrow scope.
00:12 Marco: perfect. quick round: i run the commercial side, i'm Marco — this is Sana who's our solutions engineer who will poke at the infra bits. Sana?
00:18 Sana: hey all, hi, good to meet you. i'll jump into the tech questions as we go, and we can sketch a pilot.
00:23 Priya: i am Priya, CTO. James on infra, Lara on model selection, and Tom from procurement. our main use case is a customer-support summarization + reranking pipeline that sometimes touches PII and EU data. so the compliance piece matters.
00:35 James: and we have ~200 qps peak during business hours, bursty spikes, sequence lengths around 512 tokens typical, some long-form as well.
00:42 Lara: accuracy matters — we will compare a few open models and need to measure hallucination/regression risk.
00:47 Marco: makes sense. at a high level Redwood supports three hosting paths: hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token and quick experimentation; Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput/SLAs; and Private (VPC or on-prem) for sensitive/regulatory data. i want to focus first on getting you to first request with hosted quickstart credits, then plan a pilot for dedicated or private depending on compliance.
01:02 Priya: about the credits — is there any friction to get started? we want engineers to run a smoke test without procurement getting involved.
01:08 Marco: the self-serve flow is straightforward — we give credits, you create an org, get keys. typical time-to-first-token for an engineer is under an hour, often minutes if they use our SDK. we'll send a redemption link and sample curl/SDK snippets.
01:20 Tom: will this require corporate card or procurement to sign?
01:22 Marco: for the credits no, it's self-serve. procurement only steps in for Dedicated or Private contracts.
01:28 James: network egress — our EU customers must keep data in eu-west-1. if we start hosted, can we pin region?
01:33 Sana: yes — hosted supports regional endpoints. for low-latency you can route to EU region. we also have automatic fallback routing but you can pin to region for data residency.
01:44 Priya: for PII we'd probably want private or VPC. what does the private deployment actually look like? on-prem or VPC options?
01:50 Sana: both. VPC private deployment is our common path: we deploy inference workers into your cloud account or a customer-controlled VPC with a private control plane. keys and requests never traverse our public plane. on-prem is available for air-gapped setups but has longer lead time.
02:05 Priya: KMS/HSM — we use an HSM for key material, can Redwood integrate?
02:09 Sana: yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM on private installs. we'll share the KMS integration notes. key management for Hosted uses our managed KMS but you can opt for bring-your-own in Dedicated/Private.
02:19 Lara: model onboarding: can we bring our own model or do we have to use Redwood-curated ones?
02:24 Marco: you can bring your own weights in Private, and in Dedicated we also support customer model artifacts depending on licensing. Hosted hosts a catalog of open models we verify. for POC i suggest starting with a well-known open LLM to validate latency and token costs.
02:38 Priya: benchmarks — we need predictable unit economics. how do caching and batching affect cost?
02:43 Sana: good call — our runtime supports KV/prefix caching, continuous batching, quantization profiles. caching reduces per-token cost for repeated contexts; batching improves throughput but can increase P99 latency if misconfigured. in Dedicated you can tune batching policies more aggressively.
03:00 James: do you instrument token-level cost visibility? we need per-route cost breakdown to map back to product metrics.
03:05 Marco: yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost per route/model and traces. we'll give you a demo dashboard during the pilot.
03:11 Tom: security and compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs?
03:15 Marco: hosted and Dedicated environment are SOC2 compliant; Private deployments can be configured to satisfy additional audits. we produce audit logs, access trails, and integrate with SSO/SAML for RBAC. we'll attach our compliance pack.
03:26 Priya: okay cool. on timeline — we want a quick experiment in two to three weeks then decide on Dedicated pilot in a month. is that realistic?
03:33 Marco: yes — quickstart in days with credits, pilot in 2-4 weeks once we have traffic profile to provision Dedicated nodes or schedule Private onboarding.
03:40 Lara: for the experiments we want to run A/B across model variants and measure hallucination rate, latency, and cost per 1k tokens. do you help with eval tooling?
03:48 Sana: we have a built-in eval harness and you can attach prompt sets. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching profiles based on those evals. we can export results to csv.
03:57 James: network egress costs — if we run Dedicated in your cloud region, how do we manage network egress and VPC endpoints?
04:02 Sana: with Dedicated you control the VPC; egress charges are standard cloud provider charges. for Private VPC we can use interface endpoints and avoid public internet. we'll share architecture diagrams.
04:13 Priya: how does rollback / graceful degradation work if capacity is saturated? we cannot have support chat down for hours.
04:19 Marco: we have smart routing and automatic fallback: route by latency or cost, fallback to smaller model variants or cross-region. also canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies in the Console.
04:29 Tom: procurement — once we decide on Dedicated, what are typical contract lengths and commitments?
04:33 Marco: Dedicated is typically monthly or annual reserved capacity. we provide burst options for spikes. i'll send a draft contract sample.
04:40 Priya: about the quickstart, can we run the summarization pipeline end-to-end, including embeddings for semantic search?
04:46 Sana: yes — the API supports generation + embeddings + reranking primitives. embeddings are billed per unit; we can give sample pipelines.
04:55 Lara: dataset privacy — if we send customer transcripts to hosted for evaluation during POC, how long are they retained?
04:59 Marco: hosted default retention is 30 days for logs but we can configure retention and disable retention for sensitive payloads; Private keeps everything local to your deployment. we'll include retention options in the security doc.
05:12 James: for the pilot we'll need to script load tests. do you have a runner or should we use k6/locust?
05:17 Sana: many teams use k6; we can provide a sample k6 script that hits the SDK and collects latency and token counts. we'll also run a Redwood-side benchmark if you allow us to provision nodes.
05:26 Priya: do you have any references for financial services or health where compliance was heavy?
05:30 Marco: yes, we have a handful of customers — i'll share redacted references and case studies.
05:36 Tom: i just want to double-check: quickstart credits avoid procurement, and then if we go Dedicated procurement will be needed — correct?
05:42 Marco: correct. credits are self-serve; Dedicated/Private require contracts.
05:46 Lara: i'm curious — for model quantization recommended by Optimize, do you have accuracy regression measurements?
05:51 Sana: Optimize will show expected latency and a predicted quality delta from our regressions; but you'll want to run your own eval set to confirm. quantization sometimes affects rare-token behavior.
06:02 Priya: any gotchas for using embeddings at scale for semantic search?
06:06 Sana: watch embedding dimensionality vs indexing cost; we recommend vector DBs compatible with our embedding size, and shard your index by tenant for isolation. also consider cache hot-keys for frequently searched docs.
06:17 James: okay next steps: we will accept credits, run smoke tests, share traffic profile, and schedule a pilot benchmark.
06:23 Marco: great. i'll follow up with credits link, pricing and compliance pack. Sana will send the private checklist and k6 script.
06:30 Priya: can we line up the benchmark owners now — James and Lara will be our leads.
06:34 James: yep that works.
06:36 Lara: confirmed.
06:38 Marco: excellent. anything else from procurement, Tom?
06:41 Tom: no, i'll wait for pricing and contract skeleton. thanks.
06:45 Marco: thanks everyone. end of call.
